text: In Aristotle's analysis in Physics IV, what is the ontological status of the 'now' (to nun)?
choices: It is the smallest indivisible unit of time, an atomic instant out of which longer stretches of time are built up
It is a short but genuine duration - the felt present, with a beginning, a middle, and an end
It is not a part of time but a limit or boundary of temporal intervals, analogous to a point on a line, which both divides past from future and joins them
It is a single, fixed instant identical at every moment, in which past and future permanently coincide
explanation: Aristotle treats the now as a boundary, not a part: like a geometric point on a line it has no duration, yet it both divides past from future and connects them into a continuous whole. Option 0 is the discrete, atomic-time view Aristotle rejects (time is not composed of instants); option 1 makes the now a duration, which he denies; option 3 ignores that the now is type-identical (always 'the present') but token-different (a new moment at each time).
